newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish brisk day up sharply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish brisk day up sharply.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended sharply higher after a drop in May retail sales sparked the idea the Fed will keep monetary policy unchanged in July.
"There is no way they're going to tighten with numbers like that," a Treasury bond futures trader said.

The rally got started after the Commerce Department reported May retail sales down 0.1 percent overall and excluding auto, both below forecast. April sales were revised to down 0.9 percent overall and down 0.5 percent ex-autos.
May was the third consecutive monthly decline in retail sales, the first such string of declines in 15 years.
Traders said the report was evidence that the robust U.S. economy was showing signs of slowing.
Furthermore, many traders said the mood was optimistic about upcoming inflation data.

On Friday, May's Producer Price Index (PPI) will be released and was forecast up 0.1 percent both overall and excluding volatile food and energy sectors. In April, PPI fell 0.6 percent overall and 0.1 percent ex-food and energy.
Thursday's September T-bond rally was initially met by aggressive dealer selling below 111-15/32, but traders said those sales were well absorbed by the market.
"It absorbed it but I think (dealer selling) also prevented it from going higher," the T-bond futures trader said. "This thing could have been a lot higher."
Traders estimated that one dealer sold up to 10,000 contracts on the rally and another sold as many as 8,000. Some put the estimates much higher.
A trading desk manager on the bond floor said technical momentum, despite the early sales, kept the tone buoyant into the close.
"The market was able to sustain the higher levels achieved this morning and people are optimistic about PPI," he said.
Still, a Eurodollar broker said the short-end may have gone too far.

"It looks like they've taken a tightening out pretty much for the balance of the year," a Euro trading desk manager said. "Our view is that it's overdone and maybe you don't fight it yet, but the market's got to back off."
December Euros soared to 93.955, well above resistance at 93.88 and 93.90.
"The concensus five ticks ago was that we were too high," the desk manager said.
Also reported Thursday morning were the latest weekly jobless claims, which rose to 339,000 in the June 7 week from 338,000 in the prior week.

At the close, September T-bonds were up 25/32 at 111-12/32, 10-yr notes rose 15/32 to 108-19/32, munis rose 23/32 to 119-08/32, Sept bills were up 0.0090 point at 94.770, Dec Euros rose 0.115 to 93.930.
